newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus belt stays dry, growth slowed.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus belt stays dry, growth slowed.

text.p: Most areas of the Florida citrus belt were dry again for the week ended Nov 24, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said, with most early fruit in very good condition.
There were only a few scattered showers in isolated groves and the conditions have greatly slowed most citrus tree growth, Fass said.
According to FASS, caretakers are mowing, chopping, and discing cover crops that are tall and applying very few sprays.
Additionally, FASS estimated 344,000 boxes of Navel oranges were harvested in the week ended November 24, up from 225,000 boxes in the previous week and 259,000 boxes in the week ended November 10.
An estimated 5,209,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended November 24, up from 2,373,000 boxes the prior week and 2,048,000 boxes the week ended November 10, FASS said.
